newsitem.title: USA: Newspaper says U.S. indicts Venezuelan general.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says U.S. indicts Venezuelan general.

text.p: The former head of the Venezuelan National Guard has been indicted on drug-trafficking charges by a U.S. federal grand jury, the Miami Herald reported on Saturday.

Gen. Ramon Guillen Davila, who was once one of the CIA's most trusted sources in Venezuela, was charged in a sealed indictment with smuggling up to 22 tons of cocaine into the United States, the newspaper said.
The smuggling took place while he was chief of Venezuela's National Guard anti-drug bureau between 1987 and 1991, according to unidentified sources quoted by the newspaper.
The sealed indictment in Miami did not implicate the CIA in the drug-trafficking, the sources told the Herald.
In 1992 Guillen was arrested in Venezuela on charges of drug-trafficking, and was released several months later when the charges were revoked by a Venezuelan judge.

The CBS-TV programme "60 Minutes" broadcast a show in 1993 that linked Guillen to drug-smuggling as part of an undercover programme approved by the CIA to develop confidential sources and catch major drug figures.
A Miami grand jury began investigating Guillen in 1993 after both the CIA and the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration completed their own internal investigation, the Herald said.
